newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iranians to march against German court verdict.
newsitem.headline: Iranians to march against German court verdict.

text.p: A large number of Iranians will march to the German embassy in Tehran on Sunday to protest against a German court's verdict that Iran ordered political killings in Berlin, state-run Tehran radio said on Saturday.
"Varied sections of Tehran's population will tomorrow (Sunday) hold a march to again reiterate Islamic values and sanctities and resistance in the face of the plots of Arrogance (Western)," it said.

The radio said the demonstrators would march from Tehran university's mosque to the German embassy in protest over Thursday's verdict that Iranian leaders ordered the 1992 killings of four Kurdish dissidents in Berlin.
On Saturday, demonstrations were held in the eastern city of Semnan and the western towns of Naqadeh and Piranshahr to protest against the verdict, the radio said.

"One could perhaps say that this event (verdict) is a favour from God as nothing could have exposed the falseness of Europe's ...claims of supporting human rights, justice and civilised values," the radio said in a commentary.

The court ruling said the assassinations were ordered by a secret special operations committee whose members included Iran's president, its religious leader, intelligence minister and the head of foreign policy.

But it stopped short of explicitly naming Iranian President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani and spiritual leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, whom prosecutors had accused of ultimate responsibility for the attack in Berlin's Mykonos restaurant.
Iran has repeatedly denied all involvement in the killings, which it blames on infighting among opposition groups.
European Union (EU) members, with the exception of Greece, recalled their envoys for consultations following Thursday's verdict, triggering a diplomatic row.
The radio read statements by several labour, women, student and religious organisations calling on people to take part in Sunday's scheduled protest march.
Iranian newspapers on Saturday condemned the verdict as baseless and said it was a plot hatched by arch enemies the United States and Israel.

"We are sure that Zionists and pro-Zionist Americans have a deep-rooted plot to create a big Gulf between Iran and the EU. Right now they have succeeded in their nasty mission," said the English-language Iran News.

"But the leaders of the EU should not lose their heads and try to see the other side of the coin as well. The present crisis, like the previous ones, will disappear, but Iran would now be in a better position to go after real friends for future lucrative business and commercial ties," it added.
The Tehran Times warned that the court's ruling could hurt Bonn's interests in the oil-rich Gulf region.

"Bonn should not allow a biased court to disturb its vital interests in the two sensitive regions of the Persian Gulf and Central Asia. It is not possible to have an easy access to Central Asia and Persian Gulf without Iran," it said.
On Friday, hundreds of slogan-chanting Iranians pelted the German embassy in Tehran with tomatoes.
Rafsanjani on Friday criticised the verdict but said the diplomatic row was a "passing storm" provoked by the United States and Israel.

Germany, until recently Iran's largest trading partner and most important Western friend, ordered four Iranian diplomats to the leave the country and recalled its ambassador in Tehran immediately after the court verdict. Iran also recalled its ambassador and expelled four German diplomats.
